Arrays.explanation: An array in Java is a fixed-size collection of elements of the same data type. Java provides built-in array syntax as well as the java.util.Arrays utility class, which contains methods for sorting, searching, comparing, filling, copying, converting, and manipulating arrays.

Array Introduction.explanation: An array stores multiple values of the same type in a single variable. Array indexes start from 0 and the size of an array is fixed after creation.
Array Introduction.example: An int array can store marks of multiple students.
points_to_remember: Array indexing starts from 0.
Array size is fixed after creation.
All elements normally have the same data type.
Use length to get the number of elements.
The last index is length - 1.

Array Declaration and Initialization.explanation: Java supports several ways to declare and initialize arrays.
Array Declaration and Initialization.example: new int[5] creates an integer array containing five default values.
points_to_remember: new int[5] creates an array of size 5.
Integer arrays are initialized with 0.
Boolean arrays are initialized with false.
Reference-type arrays are initialized with null.
Array literals can be used during declaration and initialization.

Array Traversal.explanation: Array elements can be accessed using traditional for loops, enhanced for loops, or other iteration mechanisms.
Array Traversal.example: A loop can be used to calculate the total of all elements in an array.
points_to_remember: Use index-based loops when the index is required.
Enhanced for loops are useful when only values are required.
Array length is accessed using the length field.
Do not access an index outside the valid range.

Arrays.toString().explanation: Arrays.toString() converts a one-dimensional array into a readable string representation.
points_to_remember: toString() is useful for displaying one-dimensional arrays.
It returns a String representation.
Use deepToString() for nested arrays.

Arrays.deepToString().explanation: deepToString() converts multidimensional or nested arrays into a readable string representation.
points_to_remember: deepToString() is designed for nested arrays.
It is useful for displaying multidimensional arrays.
Regular toString() does not provide the same readable output for nested arrays.

Arrays.sort().explanation: Arrays.sort() sorts the elements of an array into ascending order.
points_to_remember: sort() modifies the original array.
Primitive arrays are sorted in ascending order.
sort() can also sort a specified range.
Objects can be sorted according to their natural ordering or a comparator.

Arrays.parallelSort().explanation: parallelSort() sorts array elements using parallel processing when appropriate. It is useful for larger arrays where parallel execution can provide performance benefits.
Arrays.parallelSort().example: The array is sorted into ascending order using the parallel sorting implementation.
points_to_remember: parallelSort() sorts arrays in ascending order by default.
It may use multiple threads internally.
It is particularly intended for larger arrays.
It modifies the original array.

Arrays.sort() with Range.explanation: Arrays.sort() can sort only a selected range of an array. The starting index is inclusive and the ending index is exclusive.
points_to_remember: The from-index is inclusive.
The to-index is exclusive.
Elements outside the range remain unchanged.
The specified range must be valid.

Arrays.binarySearch().explanation: binarySearch() searches for an element in a sorted array using binary search and returns its index when found.
Arrays.binarySearch().example: The method returns 2 because 30 is located at index 2.
points_to_remember: The array should be sorted before binarySearch() is used.
The method returns the index when the element is found.
If the element is not found, it returns a negative value.
binarySearch() is generally faster than linear search for sorted arrays.

Arrays.binarySearch() with Range.explanation: binarySearch() can search within a specific range of a sorted array.
Arrays.binarySearch() with Range.example: The search is performed only between indexes 1 and 3.
points_to_remember: The start index is inclusive.
The end index is exclusive.
The specified range must be sorted for reliable results.

Arrays.equals().explanation: Arrays.equals() compares two one-dimensional arrays and returns true when they contain the same elements in the same order.
Arrays.equals().example: The result is true because both arrays contain the same elements in the same order.
points_to_remember: equals() compares array contents.
Order matters.
Arrays with different lengths are not equal.
Use deepEquals() for nested arrays.

Arrays.deepEquals().explanation: deepEquals() compares nested or multidimensional arrays based on their contents.
Arrays.deepEquals().example: The result is true because both nested arrays contain equivalent elements.
points_to_remember: deepEquals() supports nested arrays.
It compares nested contents recursively.
It is useful for multidimensional arrays.

Arrays.fill().explanation: Arrays.fill() assigns the same value to every element of an array.
points_to_remember: fill() replaces every element with the specified value.
It modifies the original array.
A range can also be supplied.

Arrays.fill() with Range.explanation: The range version of fill() assigns a value only to the specified portion of an array.
points_to_remember: The starting index is inclusive.
The ending index is exclusive.
Only the specified range is modified.

Arrays.copyOf().explanation: copyOf() creates a new array with the specified length and copies elements from the original array.
points_to_remember: copyOf() creates a new array.
The original array is not modified.
If the new length is larger, remaining primitive elements get default values.
If the new length is smaller, extra elements are removed.

Arrays.copyOfRange().explanation: copyOfRange() copies a selected range of an array into a new array.
points_to_remember: The start index is inclusive.
The end index is exclusive.
The result is a new array.
The original array remains unchanged.

Arrays.mismatch().explanation: mismatch() finds the index of the first position where two arrays differ. If they are equal, it returns -1.
Arrays.mismatch().example: The result is 2 because the first difference occurs at index 2.
points_to_remember: Returns the first mismatching index.
Returns -1 when arrays are equal.
Useful for comparing arrays efficiently.

Arrays.compare().explanation: compare() performs a lexicographical comparison between two arrays and returns a negative, zero, or positive integer.
Arrays.compare().example: Because 3 is smaller than 4 at the first differing position, the result is negative.
points_to_remember: Returns 0 when arrays are equal.
Returns a negative value when the first array is lexicographically smaller.
Returns a positive value when the first array is lexicographically larger.
Comparison is based on the first differing element.

Arrays.compareUnsigned().explanation: compareUnsigned() compares arrays lexicographically while treating integral values as unsigned.
Arrays.compareUnsigned().example: The comparison treats integer values using unsigned semantics rather than normal signed comparison.
points_to_remember: Useful for unsigned comparison of supported integral array types.
The result follows lexicographical comparison rules.
It differs from normal signed comparison.

Arrays.stream().explanation: Arrays.stream() creates a Java Stream from an array, allowing functional-style operations such as filter, map, sum, average, min, and max.
Arrays.stream().example: A stream can calculate the sum of all integer elements.
points_to_remember: stream() creates a stream from an array.
Streams support functional-style processing.
Primitive arrays can create IntStream, LongStream, or DoubleStream.
Stream operations do not normally modify the original array.

Arrays.asList().explanation: Arrays.asList() converts an object array into a fixed-size List backed by the original array.
Arrays.asList().example: A String array can be viewed as a List for convenient list-style operations.
points_to_remember: asList() works with object arrays.
The resulting list has fixed size.
set() can modify an existing position and affects the backing array.
add() and remove() are not supported.
For a fully modifiable ArrayList, create a new ArrayList from the result.

Arrays.hashCode().explanation: hashCode() calculates a hash code based on the contents of a one-dimensional array.
Arrays.hashCode().example: The method generates a content-based hash code for the array.
points_to_remember: hashCode() is based on array contents.
Two equal arrays produce the same content-based hash code.
Use deepHashCode() for nested arrays.

Arrays.deepHashCode().explanation: deepHashCode() generates a hash code based on the contents of nested arrays.
Arrays.deepHashCode().example: The method generates a content-based hash code for a multidimensional array.
points_to_remember: deepHashCode() supports nested arrays.
It recursively calculates hash values.
Equal nested arrays have the same deep hash code.

Arrays.setAll().explanation: setAll() sets every element of an array using a generator function based on the element's index.
points_to_remember: setAll() uses an index-based generator.
The original array is modified.
It accepts an IntUnaryOperator for int arrays.
It is useful for generating calculated array values.

Arrays.parallelSetAll().explanation: parallelSetAll() sets all elements using a generator function and may perform the operation in parallel.
points_to_remember: parallelSetAll() can use parallel execution.
The generator receives the array index.
The original array is modified.
The generator should be safe for concurrent execution.

Arrays.parallelPrefix().explanation: parallelPrefix() cumulatively applies an operation to array elements and can perform the computation in parallel.
points_to_remember: parallelPrefix() computes cumulative results.
The operation is applied from left to right.
It modifies the original array.
It can use parallel execution.

Arrays.compare() with Range.explanation: Arrays.compare() also provides overloads that compare selected ranges of two arrays.
Arrays.compare() with Range.example: Only the selected ranges are compared.
points_to_remember: Range comparison uses inclusive start and exclusive end indexes.
Only the selected portions are compared.
The result follows lexicographical comparison rules.

Multidimensional Arrays.explanation: Java supports arrays of arrays, commonly used to represent matrices and other multidimensional structures.
Multidimensional Arrays.example: A two-dimensional array can represent rows and columns of a matrix.
points_to_remember: Java multidimensional arrays are arrays of arrays.
Rows can have different lengths.
Use deepToString() to print nested arrays.
Use deepEquals() to compare nested arrays.

Object Arrays.explanation: Arrays can store references to objects, including String and custom class objects.
Object Arrays.example: A String array can store names of multiple users.
points_to_remember: Arrays can contain objects.
Reference arrays store references to objects.
Object arrays can be sorted using suitable ordering or comparators.
The array type determines which references can be stored.

Array to ArrayList.explanation: An object array can be converted into a mutable ArrayList using Arrays.asList() together with the ArrayList constructor.
Array to ArrayList.example: A fixed-size array can be converted into a resizable ArrayList.
points_to_remember: Arrays.asList() alone returns a fixed-size list.
new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(array)) creates a resizable list.
Changes to the new ArrayList do not modify the original array.

Array Index Validation.explanation: Java provides methods in the Arrays class for checking ranges and indexes in certain APIs. Invalid indexes can also cause exceptions such as ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Array Index Validation.example: Accessing numbers[3] would cause an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException because the valid indexes are 0 through 2.
points_to_remember: Valid indexes range from 0 to length - 1.
Accessing an invalid index throws an exception.
Always check array boundaries when using indexes.

summary: Arrays store multiple values of the same type.
The length field gives the number of elements.
Arrays.fill() fills an array with a specified value.
Arrays.copyOf() and copyOfRange() create new arrays from existing arrays.
Arrays.toString() and deepToString() provide readable array representations.
Arrays.mismatch() finds the first differing position.
Arrays.asList() provides a fixed-size list view for object arrays.
Arrays.parallelSetAll() and parallelPrefix() support parallel array operations.
The java.util.Arrays class contains most commonly used utility methods for arrays.
